eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 22 · Joining Tables

code:
SELECT p.Name, p.ListPrice, sod.OrderQty
FROM Production.Product AS p
INNER JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS sod
    ON p.ProductID = sod.ProductID;
caption: ON is the predicate that decides which rows from each table get paired.

steps.label: MATCHED
steps.sub: row exists on both sides — kept

steps.label: UNMATCHED
steps.sub: row exists on only one side — dropped

eyebrow: WHERE still works after a JOIN
code:
SELECT p.Name, p.ListPrice, sod.OrderQty
FROM Production.Product AS p
INNER JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS sod
    ON p.ProductID = sod.ProductID
WHERE p.Color = 'Red'
ORDER BY sod.OrderQty DESC;
caption: WHERE filters the already-joined, combined rows.

subtitle: Keeping the unmatched rows INNER JOIN throws away.
